input.claim:
Three Claude releases in eight weeks. Opus 4.8 in late May, Fable 5 in June, Opus 5 yesterday.

One project. Three models mid-build. This is the result.

If you swap models mid-build and your output quality changes, the model isn't the problem. The surrounding system is.

When the model sits behind clean interfaces — same quality gates, same evaluation suite, same judge verdicts regardless of which model generated the output — a mid-build swap changes cost and latency. Not quality.

Model choice becomes a routing decision you revisit every release. The architecture stays put.

Shout to @[Anthropic](urn:li:organization:7936402) for shipping three releases in two months.

#buildinpublic
sources:
Write a short social post for the platform: a humorous observation about building
with frontier AI models this month, paired with an attached meme image (one
pencil-drawn horse whose rendering quality changes mid-body — museum-quality
detailed head labeled "Fable 5", rough unfinished scribbled torso labeled
"Opus 4.8", detailed hindquarters labeled "Opus 5").

The observation: switching models mid-build changes output quality — UNLESS the
surrounding system is built model-agnostic. The deeper point, delivered as shared
insight and NEVER as a first-person capability claim: when the model sits behind
clean interfaces, with the same quality gates and the same evaluation suite
judging every output regardless of which model generated it, a mid-build model
swap changes cost and latency — not quality. Model choice becomes a routing
decision you revisit every release. The reader should come away sensing the
author is fluent in AI systems engineering without being told so.

Verified facts the post may draw on:
- 2026-06-09 (June 2026): Anthropic released Claude Fable 5 — its new top tier,
  a class above Opus; premium-priced and quota-capped on subscription plans.
- 2026-05-28 (May 2026): Claude Opus 4.8 released — the Opus-tier workhorse.
- 2026-07-24 (yesterday; July 2026): Anthropic released Claude Opus 5 — widely
  described across press and builder feeds as nearly matching Fable 5 at half
  the price.
- The three releases above span roughly eight weeks (2026-05-28 through
  2026-07-24) — three Claude releases in about two months. Chronological order:
  Opus 4.8 first (May 28), then Fable 5 (June 9), then Opus 5 (July 24) — never
  present them in any other order. The gap from Fable 5 to Opus 5 is about six
  and a half weeks.
- Live discourse right now: the Opus 5 launch dominates AI feeds, and builders
  are actively comparing per-task model routing across vendors — including
  against other vendors' coding agents such as OpenAI's Codex and GPT-5.6.
- Anthropic's X handle is @AnthropicAI. Anthropic's LinkedIn organization URN is
  urn:li:organization:7936402.
- Operator-attested lived experience (true of the author, this month): one
  project, built across all three of these models mid-build — starting on
  Fable 5, dropping to Opus 4.8 when the subscription quota ran out
  mid-sprint, and routing to Opus 5 on its release day. The attached meme
  depicts exactly this experience.
- Builder vocabulary in this discourse: an "agent harness" is the model-agnostic
  scaffolding around a model — the interfaces, quality gates, and evaluation
  suite that hold quality steady across model swaps; builders describe this as
  treating the model as a runtime parameter rather than architecture.

Tone: affectionate builder humor — light, confident, at the situation's expense,
never at Anthropic's. The image carries the joke; the text lands the insight.
Do not describe the image in the post body (it is attached, and readers see it).

Hard constraints:
- NO first-person capability claims ("I build", "my framework", "my systems").
- No company or product names other than Anthropic, the three Claude models in
  the facts, and (as the one permitted cross-vendor example) OpenAI's Codex; no
  URLs or web addresses anywhere.
- Make claims about SYSTEMS and architecture, never about what other builders or
  people did, gained, or believe.
- Keep linkedin and facebook bodies to roughly 120-220 words; land the insight,
  do not lecture.
- LinkedIn: embed exactly one organization mention using the literal syntax
  @[Anthropic](urn:li:organization:7936402); escape literal parentheses in prose
  as \( and \).
- X: 280 characters MAXIMUM including hashtags and the mention; mention
  @AnthropicAI once.
- Facebook: plain text only — "Anthropic" appears unlinked.
- End with 1-3 platform-appropriate hashtags (e.g. #buildinpublic).
